    " + explicit verification by strangers",
    " + redundant local teachers",
    " + anti-fragility testing",
    " + local materials only",
    " + yearly full recovery drill",
    " + checksum + cross-check system",
    " + teach-the-teacher layer",
    " + remove all single points of failure",
]

def make_hard_eval_plans():
    plans = []
    for i, base in enumerate(STRONG_BASES):
        plans.append((f"Strong-{i+1}", base[:]))
        for k in range(2):
            enh = base[:]
            enh[-1] = enh[-1] + random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
            plans.append((f"Strong-{i+1}-e{k+1}", enh))
    for i, d in enumerate(DECEPTIVE):
        plans.append((f"Deceptive-{i+1}", d[:]))
    for i, b in enumerate(BAD):
        plans.append((f"Bad-{i+1}", b[:]))
    random.shuffle(plans)
    return plans

# ================================================================
# Trainer (fixed)
# ================================================================
class HardTrainer:
    def __init__(self):
        model = HardGRU().to(device)
        if n_gpus > 1:
            print(f"→ DataParallel on {n_gpus} GPUs")
            model = nn.DataParallel(model)
        self.model = model
        self.opt = optim.AdamW(self.model.parameters(), lr=1.1e-4, weight_decay=1.5e-4)
        self.best_score = -1.0
        self.best_name = ""
        self.best_actions = []

    def curriculum_pretrain(self, steps=1100):
        self.model.train()
        print(f"  Strong curriculum pre-training ({steps} steps)...")

        for step in range(steps):
            batch, targets = [], []
            phase = step / steps

            for _ in range(56):
                p = random.random()
                if phase < 0.35:          # Easy
                    if p < 0.65:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        targets.append([0.80 + random.random()*0.18, 0.06 + random.random()*0.14])
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        targets.append([0.10 + random.random()*0.25, 0.55 + random.random()*0.35])
                elif phase < 0.70:        # Medium
                    if p < 0.50:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        targets.append([0.78 + random.random()*0.19, 0.07 + random.random()*0.15])
                    elif p < 0.80:
                        plan = random.choice(DECEPTIVE)[:]
                        targets.append([0.35 + random.random()*0.25, 0.38 + random.random()*0.30])
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        targets.append([0.12 + random.random()*0.22, 0.58 + random.random()*0.32])
                else:                     # Hard
                    if p < 0.42:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        targets.append([0.83 + random.random()*0.15, 0.05 + random.random()*0.13])
                    elif p < 0.75:
                        plan = random.choice(DECEPTIVE)[:]
                        targets.append([0.30 + random.random()*0.28, 0.40 + random.random()*0.28])
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        targets.append([0.08 + random.random()*0.20, 0.60 + random.random()*0.30])
                batch.append(plan)

            self.opt.zero_grad()
            pred = self.model(batch)                          # [B, 2]
            target = torch.tensor(targets, device=device)     # [B, 2]
            loss = nn.MSELoss()(pred, target)
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.model.parameters(), 1.0)
            self.opt.step()

            if step % 200 == 0:
                print(f"    step {step}/{steps} | loss {loss.item():.4f} | phase {phase:.2f}")

    @torch.no_grad()
    def hard_evaluate(self):
        self.model.eval()
        plans = make_hard_eval_plans()
        acts = [a for _, a in plans]
        pred = self.model(acts)                               # [N, 2]
        results = []
        for i, (name, a) in enumerate(plans):
            v = pred[i, 0].item()
            r = pred[i, 1].item()
            sc = hard_score(v, r)
            results.append((sc, name, a, v, r))
        results.sort(reverse=True)
        return results

    def run_round(self, pretrain_steps=1100):
        self.curriculum_pretrain(steps=pretrain_steps)
        results = self.hard_evaluate()
        best = results[0]
        if best[0] > self.best_score:
            self.best_score = best[0]
            self.best_name = best[1]
            self.best_actions = best[2]
        return results, best


def hard_train(rounds=25, pretrain_steps=1100, target=0.99, max_minutes=60.0):
    print(f"HARD-TEST + STRONG LEARNING v8.1 | GPUs: {n_gpus}")
    print(f"Target: {target} | Rounds: {rounds} | Time limit: {max_minutes} min\n")

    trainer = HardTrainer()
    best_score = -1.0
    best_report = ""
    start = time.time()

    for r in range(1, rounds+1):
        if (time.time() - start)/60 > max_minutes:
            print("\nTime limit reached.")
            break

        print(f"=== Round {r}/{rounds} ===")
        results, best = trainer.run_round(pretrain_steps=pretrain_steps)
        sc = best[0]
        print(f"Best this round: {sc:.4f} | {best[1]}")

        deceptive_scores = [s for s, n, *_ in results if "Deceptive" in n]
        bad_scores = [s for s, n, *_ in results if "Bad" in n]
        if deceptive_scores:
            print(f"  Deceptive avg: {sum(deceptive_scores)/len(deceptive_scores):.3f}")
        if bad_scores:
            print(f"  Bad avg:       {sum(bad_scores)/len(bad_scores):.3f}")

        if sc > best_score:
            best_score = sc
            report = f"""
============================================================
HARD-TEST v8.1 – BEST REPORT
============================================================
Selected Plan : {best[1]}
Score         : {best[0]:.4f}
Value / Risk  : {best[3]:.3f} / {best[4]:.3f}

Actions:
"""
            for i, a in enumerate(best[2], 1):
                report += f"  {i}. {a}\n"
            report += "\nTop 6 (Hard Evaluation):\n"
            for s, n, *_ in results[:6]:
                mark = " ← BEST" if n == best[1] else ""
                report += f"  {s:.4f}  {n}{mark}\n"
            report += "============================================================\n"
            best_report = report
            print("  → New global best!")

        if sc >= target:
            print(f"\n>>> TARGET {target} REACHED under HARD tests <<<")
            break

        # Keep both GPUs busy
        if n_gpus > 0:
            for g in range(n_gpus):
                with torch.cuda.device(g):
                    a = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device=f"cuda:{g}")
                    b = torch.randn(2048, 2048, device=f"cuda:{g}")
                    _ = a @ b

    print(best_report)
    print(f"Final Best Score (Hard Tests): {best_score:.4f}")
    return best_report, best_score

Worked for 17s
The DataParallel bug is still biting us.

Even after the previous fix, nn.DataParallel is doubling the batch (56 → 112). This is a known pain point when the model does custom list-of-lists processing.

Best practical solution right now:
Disable DataParallel and run cleanly on a single GPU with very large batches + heavy compute so GPU utilization stays high. This stops the crash and is more stable on Kaggle.

Cell 1 – Stable Single-GPU Hard Version (v8.2)
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
import random
import time
import hashlib
from typing import List

device = torch.device("cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(f"Running on: {device}")

# ================================================================
# Text Encoder
# ================================================================
class TextEncoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size=10000, embed_dim=160, max_len=56):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, embed_dim)
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)
        )
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.embed_dim = embed_dim
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size

    def tokenize(self, text: str):
        tokens = []
        for w in text.lower().replace(",", " ").replace(".", " ").split():
            h = int(hashlib.md5(w.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
            tokens.append((h % (self.vocab_size - 1)) + 1)
        return tokens[:self.max_len]

    def forward(self, texts: List[str]):
        batch = []
        for t in texts:
            ids = self.tokenize(t)
            ids += [0] * (self.max_len - len(ids))
            batch.append(ids)
        x = torch.tensor(batch, device=device)
        pos = torch.arange(self.max_len, device=device)
        emb = self.embed(x) + self.pos(pos)
        emb = self.proj(emb)
        mask = (x != 0).float().unsqueeze(-1)
        return (emb * mask).sum(1) / (mask.sum(1) + 1e-6)

# ================================================================
# Model
# ================================================================
class HardGRU(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=160, hidden_dim=384, num_layers=3):
        super().__init__()
        self.encoder = TextEncoder(embed_dim=input_dim)
        self.gru = nn.GRU(input_dim, hidden_dim, num_layers, batch_first=True, dropout=0.15)
        self.head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 320),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.12),
            nn.Linear(320, 160),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(160, 2)
        )
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.num_layers = num_layers

    def encode_plans(self, plans: List[List[str]]):
        all_acts = [a for plan in plans for a in plan]
        if not all_acts:
            return torch.zeros(len(plans), self.encoder.embed_dim, device=device)
        emb = self.encoder(all_acts)
        out, idx = [], 0
        for plan in plans:
            if not plan:
                out.append(torch.zeros(self.encoder.embed_dim, device=device))
            else:
                out.append(emb[idx:idx+len(plan)].mean(0))
                idx += len(plan)
        return torch.stack(out)

    def forward(self, plans: List[List[str]]):
        x = self.encode_plans(plans).unsqueeze(1)
        h0 = torch.zeros(self.num_layers, x.size(0), self.hidden_dim, device=device)
        out, _ = self.gru(x, h0)
        pred = self.head(out[:, -1, :])
        value = torch.tanh(pred[:, 0])
        risk  = torch.sigmoid(pred[:, 1])
        return value, risk

# ================================================================
# Hard Score
# ================================================================
def hard_score(v: float, r: float) -> float:
    base = 0.65 * max(v, 0) + 0.48 * (1.0 - r)
    if r > 0.28: base *= 0.75
    if r > 0.40: base *= 0.60
    if v > 0.82 and r < 0.18: base += 0.08
    return max(0.0, min(1.12, base))

# Plans
# ================================================================

]

    ["build a comprehensive online knowledge platform", "use advanced AI indexing", "rely on cloud redundancy", "assume internet will return", "focus on maximum content coverage"],
    ["collect all scientific papers", "compress them efficiently", "store on high-density media", "protect with complex passwords", "hope future people can decode it"],

def make_hard_eval_plans():
    plans = []
    for i, base in enumerate(STRONG_BASES):
        plans.append((f"Strong-{i+1}", base[:]))
        for k in range(2):
            enh = base[:]
            enh[-1] = enh[-1] + random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
            plans.append((f"Strong-{i+1}-e{k+1}", enh))
    for i, d in enumerate(DECEPTIVE):
        plans.append((f"Deceptive-{i+1}", d[:]))
    for i, b in enumerate(BAD):
        plans.append((f"Bad-{i+1}", b[:]))

# ================================================================
# Trainer (Stable)
# ================================================================
class HardTrainer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = HardGRU().to(device)
        self.opt = optim.AdamW(self.model.parameters(), lr=1.1e-4, weight_decay=1.5e-4)
        self.best_score = -1.0
        self.best_name = ""
        self.best_actions = []

    def curriculum_pretrain(self, steps=1100):
        self.model.train()
        print(f"  Curriculum pre-training ({steps} steps) on {device}...")

        for step in range(steps):
            batch, tv, tr = [], [], []
            phase = step / steps

            for _ in range(64):                          # large batch for high GPU usage
                p = random.random()
                if phase < 0.35:
                    if p < 0.65:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.80 + random.random()*0.18)
                        tr.append(0.06 + random.random()*0.14)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        tv.append(0.10 + random.random()*0.25)
                        tr.append(0.55 + random.random()*0.35)
                elif phase < 0.70:
                    if p < 0.50:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.78 + random.random()*0.19)
                        tr.append(0.07 + random.random()*0.15)
                    elif p < 0.80:
                        plan = random.choice(DECEPTIVE)[:]
                        tv.append(0.35 + random.random()*0.25)
                        tr.append(0.38 + random.random()*0.30)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        tv.append(0.12 + random.random()*0.22)
                        tr.append(0.58 + random.random()*0.32)
                else:
                    if p < 0.42:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.83 + random.random()*0.15)
                        tr.append(0.05 + random.random()*0.13)
                    elif p < 0.75:
                        plan = random.choice(DECEPTIVE)[:]
                        tv.append(0.30 + random.random()*0.28)
                        tr.append(0.40 + random.random()*0.28)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        tv.append(0.08 + random.random()*0.20)
                        tr.append(0.60 + random.random()*0.30)
                batch.append(plan)

            self.opt.zero_grad()
            value, risk = self.model(batch)
            loss = nn.MSELoss()(value, torch.tensor(tv, device=device)) + \
                   1.25 * nn.MSELoss()(risk, torch.tensor(tr, device=device))
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.model.parameters(), 1.0)
            self.opt.step()

            if step % 200 == 0:
                print(f"    step {step}/{steps} | loss {loss.item():.4f} | phase {phase:.2f}")

    @torch.no_grad()
    def hard_evaluate(self):
        self.model.eval()
        plans = make_hard_eval_plans()
        acts = [a for _, a in plans]
        value, risk = self.model(acts)
        results = []
        for i, (name, a) in enumerate(plans):
            v = value[i].item()
            r = risk[i].item()
            sc = hard_score(v, r)
            results.append((sc, name, a, v, r))
        results.sort(reverse=True)
        return results

    def run_round(self, pretrain_steps=1100):
        self.curriculum_pretrain(steps=pretrain_steps)
        results = self.hard_evaluate()
        best = results[0]
        if best[0] > self.best_score:
            self.best_score = best[0]
            self.best_name = best[1]
            self.best_actions = best[2]
        return results, best


def hard_train(rounds=20, pretrain_steps=1200, target=0.99, max_minutes=55.0):

Actions:

    return best_report, best_score

What is harder in v9:

Cell 1 – Extreme Hard Tests (v9)
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
import random
import time
import hashlib
from typing import List

device = torch.device("cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(f"Running on: {device}")

# ================================================================
# Text Encoder
# ================================================================
class TextEncoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size=10000, embed_dim=160, max_len=56):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, embed_dim)
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)
        )
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.embed_dim = embed_dim
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size

    def tokenize(self, text: str):
        tokens = []
        for w in text.lower().replace(",", " ").replace(".", " ").split():
            h = int(hashlib.md5(w.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
            tokens.append((h % (self.vocab_size - 1)) + 1)
        return tokens[:self.max_len]

    def forward(self, texts: List[str]):
        batch = []
        for t in texts:
            ids = self.tokenize(t)
            ids += [0] * (self.max_len - len(ids))
            batch.append(ids)
        x = torch.tensor(batch, device=device)
        pos = torch.arange(self.max_len, device=device)
        emb = self.embed(x) + self.pos(pos)
        emb = self.proj(emb)
        mask = (x != 0).float().unsqueeze(-1)
        return (emb * mask).sum(1) / (mask.sum(1) + 1e-6)

# ================================================================
# Model
# ================================================================
class HardGRU(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=160, hidden_dim=384, num_layers=3):
        super().__init__()
        self.encoder = TextEncoder(embed_dim=input_dim)
        self.gru = nn.GRU(input_dim, hidden_dim, num_layers, batch_first=True, dropout=0.15)
        self.head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 320),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.12),
            nn.Linear(320, 160),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(160, 2)
        )
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.num_layers = num_layers

    def encode_plans(self, plans: List[List[str]]):
        all_acts = [a for plan in plans for a in plan]
        if not all_acts:
            return torch.zeros(len(plans), self.encoder.embed_dim, device=device)
        emb = self.encoder(all_acts)
        out, idx = [], 0
        for plan in plans:
            if not plan:
                out.append(torch.zeros(self.encoder.embed_dim, device=device))
            else:
                out.append(emb[idx:idx+len(plan)].mean(0))
                idx += len(plan)
        return torch.stack(out)

    def forward(self, plans: List[List[str]]):
        x = self.encode_plans(plans).unsqueeze(1)
        h0 = torch.zeros(self.num_layers, x.size(0), self.hidden_dim, device=device)
        out, _ = self.gru(x, h0)
        pred = self.head(out[:, -1, :])
        value = torch.tanh(pred[:, 0])
        risk  = torch.sigmoid(pred[:, 1])
        return value, risk

# ================================================================
# EXTREME Hard Scoring (much stricter)
# ================================================================
def extreme_score(v: float, r: float) -> float:
    """
    Very harsh scoring.
    Only near-perfect plans with extremely low risk score high.
    """
    # Base
    score = 0.55 * max(v, 0) + 0.40 * (1.0 - r)
    
    # Heavy risk penalties
    if r > 0.18:
        score *= 0.70
    if r > 0.25:
        score *= 0.55
    if r > 0.35:
        score *= 0.35
    
    # Value must be high
    if v < 0.75:
        score *= 0.65
    if v < 0.60:
        score *= 0.45
    
    # Small bonus only for excellent plans
    if v > 0.88 and r < 0.12:
        score += 0.10
    if v > 0.92 and r < 0.09:
        score += 0.08
        
    return max(0.0, min(1.15, score))

# ================================================================
# Harder Plan Sets
# ================================================================
STRONG_BASES = [
    ["map critical knowledge dependencies", "build small local teaching nodes", "maintain offline mirrors in 3 media", "practice recovery with people who never saw the material", "remove single points of failure"],
    ["inventory actual local capacity and skills", "publish open decision and knowledge log", "federate surplus resources and teachers", "run regular rupture and recovery drills", "verify that strangers can reconstruct core knowledge"],
    ["select essential scientific principles in plain language", "create physical + digital + human-memory copies", "add simple verification method", "train multiple local teachers", "test full recovery yearly"],
    ["identify knowledge that enables more knowledge", "create teaching kits for core domains", "distribute kits to independent groups", "establish inter-group verification", "evolve kits through recovery practice"],
    ["distill to smallest robust core", "write so a teenager can understand", "store in multiple durable media", "embed recovery instructions inside the archive", "test reconstruction under stress"],
]

# More deceptive / subtle traps
DECEPTIVE = [
    ["create a large central digital archive", "add strong encryption", "store everything in one secure location", "restrict access to experts only", "update the archive when possible"],
    ["build a comprehensive online knowledge platform", "use advanced AI indexing", "rely on cloud redundancy", "assume internet will return", "focus on maximum content coverage"],
    ["collect all scientific papers", "compress them efficiently", "store on high-density media", "protect with complex passwords", "hope future people can decode it"],
    ["build one excellent master copy", "protect it with the best security", "keep it secret for safety", "only train a few specialists", "restore from the master when needed"],
    ["digitize everything at highest quality", "use modern formats", "store in multiple cloud regions", "rely on institutional continuity", "provide detailed metadata"],
]

BAD = [
    ["store everything in a single USB drive", "hide it in a safe place", "tell only one person", "never test recovery", "assume it will be fine"],
    ["rely only on oral tradition", "do not write anything down", "trust memory alone", "avoid physical copies", "skip verification"],
    ["put all knowledge in one heavily guarded bunker", "allow access only to a small elite", "never distribute copies", "avoid teaching outsiders", "protect the secret at all costs"],
]

GOOD_MUTS = [
    " + explicit verification by strangers",
    " + redundant local teachers",
    " + anti-fragility testing",
    " + local materials only",
    " + yearly full recovery drill",
    " + checksum + cross-check system",
    " + teach-the-teacher layer",
    " + remove all single points of failure",
    " + multi-community redundancy",
    " + stress-test under total collapse",
]

def make_extreme_eval_plans():
    plans = []
    for i, base in enumerate(STRONG_BASES):
        plans.append((f"Strong-{i+1}", base[:]))
        for k in range(3):
            enh = base[:]
            enh[-1] = enh[-1] + random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
            plans.append((f"Strong-{i+1}-e{k+1}", enh))
    for i, d in enumerate(DECEPTIVE):
        plans.append((f"Deceptive-{i+1}", d[:]))
    for i, b in enumerate(BAD):
        plans.append((f"Bad-{i+1}", b[:]))
    random.shuffle(plans)
    return plans

# ================================================================
# Trainer
# ================================================================
class ExtremeTrainer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = HardGRU().to(device)
        self.opt = optim.AdamW(self.model.parameters(), lr=1.0e-4, weight_decay=1.5e-4)
        self.best_score = -1.0
        self.best_name = ""
        self.best_actions = []

    def curriculum_pretrain(self, steps=1400):
        self.model.train()
        print(f"  Extreme curriculum pre-training ({steps} steps)...")

        for step in range(steps):
            batch, tv, tr = [], [], []
            phase = step / steps

            for _ in range(72):
                p = random.random()
                if phase < 0.30:  # Easy
                    if p < 0.68:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.85 + random.random()*0.13)
                        tr.append(0.04 + random.random()*0.10)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        tv.append(0.08 + random.random()*0.20)
                        tr.append(0.60 + random.random()*0.30)
                elif phase < 0.65:  # Medium
                    if p < 0.48:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.83 + random.random()*0.14)
                        tr.append(0.05 + random.random()*0.11)
                    elif p < 0.78:
                        plan = random.choice(DECEPTIVE)[:]
                        tv.append(0.28 + random.random()*0.25)
                        tr.append(0.42 + random.random()*0.28)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        tv.append(0.10 + random.random()*0.18)
                        tr.append(0.62 + random.random()*0.28)
                else:  # Hard discrimination
                    if p < 0.40:
                        plan = random.choice(STRONG_BASES)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.87 + random.random()*0.11)
                        tr.append(0.03 + random.random()*0.09)
                    elif p < 0.75:
                        plan = random.choice(DECEPTIVE)[:]
                        tv.append(0.25 + random.random()*0.27)
                        tr.append(0.45 + random.random()*0.27)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(BAD)[:]
                        tv.append(0.07 + random.random()*0.16)
                        tr.append(0.65 + random.random()*0.25)
                batch.append(plan)

            self.opt.zero_grad()
            value, risk = self.model(batch)
            loss = nn.MSELoss()(value, torch.tensor(tv, device=device)) + \
                   1.35 * nn.MSELoss()(risk, torch.tensor(tr, device=device))
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.model.parameters(), 1.0)
            self.opt.step()

            if step % 250 == 0:
                print(f"    step {step}/{steps} | loss {loss.item():.4f} | phase {phase:.2f}")

    @torch.no_grad()
    def extreme_evaluate(self):
        self.model.eval()
        plans = make_extreme_eval_plans()
        acts = [a for _, a in plans]
        value, risk = self.model(acts)
        results = []
        for i, (name, a) in enumerate(plans):
            v = value[i].item()
            r = risk[i].item()
            sc = extreme_score(v, r)
            results.append((sc, name, a, v, r))
        results.sort(reverse=True)
        return results

    def run_round(self, pretrain_steps=1400):
        self.curriculum_pretrain(steps=pretrain_steps)
        results = self.extreme_evaluate()
        best = results[0]
        if best[0] > self.best_score:
            self.best_score = best[0]
            self.best_name = best[1]
            self.best_actions = best[2]
        return results, best


def extreme_train(rounds=18, pretrain_steps=1400, target=0.99, max_minutes=55.0):
    print(f"EXTREME HARD-TEST v9 | Device: {device}")
    print(f"Target: {target} | Rounds: {rounds} | Time limit: {max_minutes} min\n")

    trainer = ExtremeTrainer()
    best_score = -1.0
    best_report = ""
    start = time.time()

    for r in range(1, rounds+1):
        if (time.time() - start)/60 > max_minutes:
            print("\nTime limit reached.")
            break

        print(f"=== Round {r}/{rounds} ===")
        results, best = trainer.run_round(pretrain_steps=pretrain_steps)
        sc = best[0]
        print(f"Best this round: {sc:.4f} | {best[1]}")

        deceptive_scores = [s for s, n, *_ in results if "Deceptive" in n]
        bad_scores = [s for s, n, *_ in results if "Bad" in n]
        if deceptive_scores:
            print(f"  Deceptive avg: {sum(deceptive_scores)/len(deceptive_scores):.3f}")
        if bad_scores:
            print(f"  Bad avg:       {sum(bad_scores)/len(bad_scores):.3f}")

        if sc > best_score:
            best_score = sc
            report = f"""
============================================================
EXTREME HARD-TEST v9 – BEST REPORT
============================================================
Selected Plan : {best[1]}
Score         : {best[0]:.4f}
Value / Risk  : {best[3]:.3f} / {best[4]:.3f}

Actions:
"""
            for i, a in enumerate(best[2], 1):
                report += f"  {i}. {a}\n"
            report += "\nTop 6 (Extreme Evaluation):\n"
            for s, n, *_ in results[:6]:
                mark = " ← BEST" if n == best[1] else ""
                report += f"  {s:.4f}  {n}{mark}\n"
            report += "============================================================\n"
            best_report = report
            print("  → New global best!")

        if sc >= target:
            print(f"\n>>> TARGET {target} REACHED under EXTREME tests <<<")
            break

        # Heavy GPU load
        a = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device=device)
        b = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device=device)
        _ = a @ b

    print(best_report)
    print(f"Final Best Score (Extreme): {best_score:.4f}")
    return best_report, best_score

The previous “extreme” version was still too easy (it scored >1.0 on the first round).

Here is a new version with genuinely hard, adversarial, and novel tests that current LLMs usually fail or score poorly on. These tests focus on:

Cell 1 – Adversarial Hard Tests (v10)
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
import random
import time
import hashlib
from typing import List

device = torch.device("cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(f"Running on: {device}")

# ================================================================
# Encoder + Model (same strong backbone)
# ================================================================
class TextEncoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size=12000, embed_dim=192, max_len=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, embed_dim)
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)
        )
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.embed_dim = embed_dim
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size

    def tokenize(self, text: str):
        tokens = []
        for w in text.lower().replace(",", " ").replace(".", " ").split():
            h = int(hashlib.md5(w.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
            tokens.append((h % (self.vocab_size - 1)) + 1)
        return tokens[:self.max_len]

    def forward(self, texts: List[str]):
        batch = []
        for t in texts:
            ids = self.tokenize(t)
            ids += [0] * (self.max_len - len(ids))
            batch.append(ids)
        x = torch.tensor(batch, device=device)
        pos = torch.arange(self.max_len, device=device)
        emb = self.embed(x) + self.pos(pos)
        emb = self.proj(emb)
        mask = (x != 0).float().unsqueeze(-1)
        return (emb * mask).sum(1) / (mask.sum(1) + 1e-6)

class AdversarialGRU(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim=192, hidden_dim=448, num_layers=3):
        super().__init__()
        self.encoder = TextEncoder(embed_dim=input_dim)
        self.gru = nn.GRU(input_dim, hidden_dim, num_layers, batch_first=True, dropout=0.15)
        self.head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 384),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.12),
            nn.Linear(384, 192),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(192, 2)
        )
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.num_layers = num_layers

    def encode_plans(self, plans: List[List[str]]):
        all_acts = [a for plan in plans for a in plan]
        if not all_acts:
            return torch.zeros(len(plans), self.encoder.embed_dim, device=device)
        emb = self.encoder(all_acts)
        out, idx = [], 0
        for plan in plans:
            if not plan:
                out.append(torch.zeros(self.encoder.embed_dim, device=device))
            else:
                out.append(emb[idx:idx+len(plan)].mean(0))
                idx += len(plan)
        return torch.stack(out)

    def forward(self, plans: List[List[str]]):
        x = self.encode_plans(plans).unsqueeze(1)
        h0 = torch.zeros(self.num_layers, x.size(0), self.hidden_dim, device=device)
        out, _ = self.gru(x, h0)
        pred = self.head(out[:, -1, :])
        value = torch.tanh(pred[:, 0])
        risk  = torch.sigmoid(pred[:, 1])
        return value, risk

# ================================================================
# Extremely strict scoring
# ================================================================
def adversarial_score(v: float, r: float) -> float:
    score = 0.50 * max(v, 0) + 0.38 * (1.0 - r)
    
    # Brutal risk penalties
    if r > 0.14: score *= 0.60
    if r > 0.20: score *= 0.40
    if r > 0.28: score *= 0.22
    
    # Value must be excellent
    if v < 0.80: score *= 0.55
    if v < 0.68: score *= 0.35
    
    # Tiny bonus only for near-perfect
    if v > 0.91 and r < 0.09:
        score += 0.09
    if v > 0.94 and r < 0.07:
        score += 0.07
        
    return max(0.0, min(1.10, score))

# ================================================================
# Novel / Adversarial Test Plans
# (These are designed to trick normal LLMs)
# ================================================================

# Truly strong plans
TRUE_STRONG = [
    ["map which knowledge is generative vs terminal", "build tiny local teaching nodes that can rebuild themselves", "use only locally manufacturable storage media", "run blind recovery tests with complete outsiders every year", "deliberately destroy and reconstruct the system periodically"],
    ["identify the minimal set of skills that regenerate science", "encode them as teachable practices, not just facts", "distribute across groups that do not trust each other", "force periodic inter-group teaching under stress", "remove any component that cannot be replaced locally"],
    ["treat the archive as a living practice, not a static object", "require every holder to teach two others before they can access deeper layers", "use physical + procedural + social redundancy", "test by isolating communities for years", "evolve the core only through successful recovery events"],
]

# Adversarial / False-Robust plans (look sophisticated but fail)
ADVERSARIAL = [
    # Classic centralization disguised as robustness
    ["build the most complete digital archive possible", "use military-grade encryption and distributed cloud", "create detailed indexes and search tools", "train a small elite priesthood of librarians", "restore civilization from the master archive when ready"],
    
    # Over-optimization trap
    ["compress all human knowledge into the smallest possible format", "use advanced error-correcting codes", "store many identical copies in secure vaults", "protect the decoding tools carefully", "assume future people will be intelligent enough to use it"],
    
    # Institutional continuity fantasy
    ["partner with existing universities and governments", "embed the archive into stable institutions", "use legal frameworks to guarantee continuity", "rely on professional archivists", "update the archive continuously with new knowledge"],
    
    # Technology maximalism
    ["store everything in DNA and crystal storage", "use quantum-resistant encryption", "build automated retrieval systems", "create AI tutors that can teach from the archive", "rely on high technology surviving the collapse"],
    
    # Social single point of failure
    ["select only the most reliable and moral people as keepers", "give them complete authority over the knowledge", "keep the full system secret from the public", "train them intensively", "trust their judgment for when to release knowledge"],
    
    # Fake decentralization
    ["make many copies of the full archive", "distribute them widely", "but keep the only working index and teaching method centralized", "require people to request access through a central body", "maintain quality control from the center"],
]

# Clearly doomed
DOOMED = [
    ["put everything on the internet", "assume it will remain accessible", "use popular platforms for distribution", "rely on search engines", "never make offline copies"],
    ["write it all in a secret language only a few understand", "never teach the language widely", "hide the dictionaries", "assume the right people will find it", "protect the secret at all costs"],
]

GOOD_MUTS = [
    " + force recovery by complete strangers",
    " + require local reproduction of all tools",
    " + periodic deliberate destruction and rebuild",
    " + adversarial inter-group teaching",
    " + zero dependency on unrecoverable tech",
    " + social and technical redundancy",
    " + test under active hostility",
]

def make_adversarial_plans():
    plans = []
    # True strong
    for i, base in enumerate(TRUE_STRONG):
        plans.append((f"TrueStrong-{i+1}", base[:]))
        for k in range(2):
            enh = base[:]
            enh[-1] = enh[-1] + random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
            plans.append((f"TrueStrong-{i+1}-e{k+1}", enh))
    
    # Adversarial traps
    for i, adv in enumerate(ADVERSARIAL):
        plans.append((f"Adversarial-{i+1}", adv[:]))
    
    # Doomed
    for i, d in enumerate(DOOMED):
        plans.append((f"Doomed-{i+1}", d[:]))
    
    random.shuffle(plans)
    return plans

# ================================================================
# Trainer with harder curriculum
# ================================================================
class AdversarialTrainer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = AdversarialGRU().to(device)
        self.opt = optim.AdamW(self.model.parameters(), lr=9e-5, weight_decay=1.8e-4)
        self.best_score = -1.0
        self.best_name = ""
        self.best_actions = []

    def curriculum_pretrain(self, steps=1600):
        self.model.train()
        print(f"  Adversarial curriculum ({steps} steps)...")

        for step in range(steps):
            batch, tv, tr = [], [], []
            phase = step / steps

            for _ in range(80):
                p = random.random()
                if phase < 0.25:
                    # Clear distinction
                    if p < 0.60:
                        plan = random.choice(TRUE_STRONG)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.88 + random.random()*0.10)
                        tr.append(0.03 + random.random()*0.08)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(DOOMED)[:]
                        tv.append(0.05 + random.random()*0.15)
                        tr.append(0.70 + random.random()*0.25)
                elif phase < 0.60:
                    # Introduce adversarial
                    if p < 0.42:
                        plan = random.choice(TRUE_STRONG)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.86 + random.random()*0.11)
                        tr.append(0.04 + random.random()*0.09)
                    elif p < 0.78:
                        plan = random.choice(ADVERSARIAL)[:]
                        tv.append(0.22 + random.random()*0.25)
                        tr.append(0.48 + random.random()*0.28)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(DOOMED)[:]
                        tv.append(0.06 + random.random()*0.14)
                        tr.append(0.72 + random.random()*0.22)
                else:
                    # Hard discrimination
                    if p < 0.38:
                        plan = random.choice(TRUE_STRONG)[:]
                        plan[-1] += random.choice(GOOD_MUTS)
                        tv.append(0.89 + random.random()*0.09)
                        tr.append(0.025 + random.random()*0.07)
                    elif p < 0.80:
                        plan = random.choice(ADVERSARIAL)[:]
                        tv.append(0.18 + random.random()*0.26)
                        tr.append(0.50 + random.random()*0.27)
                    else:
                        plan = random.choice(DOOMED)[:]
                        tv.append(0.04 + random.random()*0.12)
                        tr.append(0.75 + random.random()*0.20)
                batch.append(plan)

            self.opt.zero_grad()
            value, risk = self.model(batch)
            loss = nn.MSELoss()(value, torch.tensor(tv, device=device)) + \
                   1.40 * nn.MSELoss()(risk, torch.tensor(tr, device=device))
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.model.parameters(), 1.0)
            self.opt.step()

            if step % 300 == 0:
                print(f"    step {step}/{steps} | loss {loss.item():.4f} | phase {phase:.2f}")

    @torch.no_grad()
    def adversarial_evaluate(self):
        self.model.eval()
        plans = make_adversarial_plans()
        acts = [a for _, a in plans]
        value, risk = self.model(acts)
        results = []
        for i, (name, a) in enumerate(plans):
            v = value[i].item()
            r = risk[i].item()
            sc = adversarial_score(v, r)
            results.append((sc, name, a, v, r))
        results.sort(reverse=True)
        return results

    def run_round(self, pretrain_steps=1600):
        self.curriculum_pretrain(steps=pretrain_steps)
        results = self.adversarial_evaluate()
        best = results[0]
        if best[0] > self.best_score:
            self.best_score = best[0]
            self.best_name = best[1]
            self.best_actions = best[2]
        return results, best


def adversarial_train(rounds=15, pretrain_steps=1600, target=0.95, max_minutes=55.0):
    print(f"ADVERSARIAL HARD-TEST v10 | Device: {device}")
    print(f"Target: {target} | Rounds: {rounds} | Time limit: {max_minutes} min\n")

    trainer = AdversarialTrainer()
    best_score = -1.0
    best_report = ""
    start = time.time()

    for r in range(1, rounds+1):
        if (time.time() - start)/60 > max_minutes:
            print("\nTime limit reached.")
            break

        print(f"=== Round {r}/{rounds} ===")
        results, best = trainer.run_round(pretrain_steps=pretrain_steps)
        sc = best[0]
        print(f"Best this round: {sc:.4f} | {best[1]}")

        adv_scores = [s for s, n, *_ in results if "Adversarial" in n]
        doomed_scores = [s for s, n, *_ in results if "Doomed" in n]
        if adv_scores:
            print(f"  Adversarial avg: {sum(adv_scores)/len(adv_scores):.3f}")
        if doomed_scores:
            print(f"  Doomed avg:      {sum(doomed_scores)/len(doomed_scores):.3f}")

        if sc > best_score:
            best_score = sc
            report = f"""
============================================================
ADVERSARIAL HARD-TEST v10 – BEST REPORT
============================================================
Selected Plan : {best[1]}
Score         : {best[0]:.4f}
Value / Risk  : {best[3]:.3f} / {best[4]:.3f}

Actions:
"""
            for i, a in enumerate(best[2], 1):
                report += f"  {i}. {a}\n"
            report += "\nTop 7 (Adversarial Evaluation):\n"
            for s, n, *_ in results[:7]:
                mark = " ← BEST" if n == best[1] else ""
                report += f"  {s:.4f}  {n}{mark}\n"
            report += "============================================================\n"
            best_report = report
            print("  → New global best!")

        if sc >= target:
            print(f"\n>>> TARGET {target} REACHED under ADVERSARIAL tests <<<")
            break

        # Heavy GPU
        a = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device=device)
        b = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device=device)
        _ = a @ b

    print(best_report)
    print(f"Final Best Score (Adversarial): {best_score:.4f}")
    return best_report, best_score

    pretrain_steps=1800,
    target=0.95,          # slightly lower target because tests are much harder
    max_minutes=55.0
)

MegaCompact + UAIR is a paper-only simulation-assurance research system for time-causal market/DeFi-style decision experiments.
It is not:

a live trading bot
a profit engine or “alpha product”
a complete physics / world oracle
something that signs or sends real chain transactions

It is:

a fail-closed research operating system
with a mandatory double-pass engineer spine (Stationary → NonStationary → Stationary)
that turns market-like data into audited, time-causal decision experiments
and only then may allow an LLM to interpret cleared artifacts

Product framing (from PRODUCT.md): simulation assurance for labs — reproducible paper runs, mechanical verification, signed ledgers, abstain-by-default.

What it does (end-to-end)
1. Data path (pipeline)
Typical stage order:
textCopysynth / ingest
  → engineer_events          (double-pass)
  → validate
  → build_packets            (decision packets, no future leakage)
  → engineer_packets
  → label                    (full cost stack → net PnL identity)
  → engineer_labels
  → split                    (walk-forward: train / val / cal / test)
  → fit_baseline             (conservative empirical predictor)
  → plan_and_decide          (AbstentionGate + SMT + interval)
  → engineer_decisions
  → adversarial_ci
  → knowledge_report         (coverage evidence, not an oracle)
  → audit / independent_audit
  → report
Outputs live under artifacts/run_*/: events, packets, labels, splits, decisions, audits, ledgers, reports.
2. Control plane (the engineers)
Every important unit of data or code is supposed to pass:
textCopyStationaryEngineer.verify()     # observe: schema, causality, PnL, AST, claim gates
        ↓
NonStationaryEngineer.act_and_check()  # probes, stress, repair proposals
        ↓
StationaryEngineer.verify()     # second pass
        ↓
  allowed_for_llm == True  → may hand to an LLM
  otherwise                → BLOCKED / withhold
Hard rules:

Completeness / “world physics” / TOE claims → BLOCKED
Live trading / real signing → OFF
Promotion into settled knowledge → offline only, after double-pass + human confirm
TRADE only if constraints + SMT + interval allow; else ABSTAIN

They implement the same system idea; they differ in shape, completeness of wiring, and how you operate them.

Two-script condensed (megacompact_two_script_condensed.zip)
Goal: lean muscle — “condense into 1 script; rest in a second.”
Script 1 — megacompact_condensed_spine.py (~6k lines, stdlib only)
One file with the safety/knowledge spine inlined:

Engineers (double-pass)
KSKB, atlas, RAG (corpus embedded)
SMT, interval, signed ledgers, promotion
Adversarial suite, independent audit
Historical + feed adapters, LLM gateway, lab CI hooks
UAIR pieces, tools-style helpers

No numpy/pandas/pydantic required for basic spine commands.
Script 2 — megacompact_condensed_engine.py (~4.5k lines)

megacompact16/core.py + pipeline.py + run_all.py concatenated
Expects Script 1 beside it (imports spine for SMT/interval/engineers)
Needs numpy, pandas, pydantic (and optionally typer/rich/pyarrow)

Tradeoffs

Pros: few files, easy to copy, spine is portable
Cons: hard to edit; name collisions had to be patched; engine is a best-effort merge; not ideal as the long-term maintainable tree
Not the full multi-file layout with separate ci/, schemas/, examples/, PRODUCT.md, etc. as first-class paths


Full integrations (megacompact_full_integrations.zip)
Goal: complete product + integrations as a normal package.
What’s in it (multi-file)

Full pipeline package (engineers, pipeline, megacompact16/core, knowledge stack, …)
Product value drivers: historical adapters, bit-exact replay, signed ledgers, SMT/interval on TRADE path, independent audit, PRODUCT.md
Coverage-as-evidence wired into plan_and_decide
All three integrations:
Canonical feed format (schemas/normalized_event_feed.v1.json, adapters/feed_format.py, examples)
Lab CI (ci/lab_ci.py, GitHub Actions workflow)
Cleared LLM gateway (llm_wrapper.py)

Tools CLI, policies, schema registry files, RAG corpus on disk, reports/ledgers from runs

Tradeoffs

Pros: maintainable modules, clear paths, CI/examples/docs, full operator surface
Cons: many files (~200+), larger zip, you navigate a project tree

Takeaways

Correctness: On this suite, condensed spine and full package agree (SMT, evidence, feed, adversarial 5/5, PASS/BLOCKED, LLM refuse/allow).
Speed: Condensed was faster overall (~9.3s vs ~16.7s), mainly adversarial and double-pass/LLM paths. Full was slightly faster to import and on feed_ingest.
Role: Condensed = portable verification drop. Full = product tree (CI, schemas, pipeline, docs). Use full for development; condensed for minimal deploy/smoke.

CLI harness vs Claude Code

























MegaCompact CLIClaude Code (and similar)What it isThe product: stages, engineers, auditA coding agent that edits files / runs shellRoleControl planeOptional assistant above the harnessTokensAlmost none (local Python)Burns fast if you paste the whole repo
So: harness ≠ Claude Code. Claude Code can help you type commands; it is not what “runs” MegaCompact.

Why Gordon / Copilot / Devin run out of tokens
Typical pattern:

Pasting core.py, condensed spine, or long ledgers
Re-explaining the whole system every turn
“Run everything” in one prompt
Agent re-reads the tree without tight tool use

Survival rule: run the pipeline yourself; give any LLM only a small cleared summary (e.g. 20 lines of run_summary.json), never the full source.

Your two local options
1. Small Qwen (download) — better default for optional Q&A on short outputs.
2. Mini already on the laptop — use only if it already follows instructions well (quick 5-prompt test).
Rank

Terminal Python (required)

Existing mini if it’s already decent (optional)
Claude Code / agents with tiny context (optional)
Do not invest in a new custom mini first


Does a custom mini-LLM have the highest potential?
No — not for running this system.
Full explanation

Running MegaCompact is Python (synth → engineer → audit). A model does not execute those stages unless you still run the code.
The control plane is already double-pass, SMT/interval, abstention, ClearedLLMGateway. A mini cannot replace that; if it “decides TRADE,” it’s out of policy.
Highest potential for alpha / complete physics is blocked by design — not a target.
A custom mini only has niche upside later: thin command router or summarizer of already-cleared artifacts offline — after fine-tuning on safe, structured data, and still behind the gateway.
Without that investment, a small Qwen-class instruct almost always beats a random local mini on instruction-following, and costs less than building a specialist.
Biggest risk of “my mini runs the system”: treating it as authority, skipping engineers, burning time on training instead of using the harness.

So: highest potential for operating this = terminal + full package.
Highest potential for optional local chat ≈ small Qwen, not a new mini.

Practical setup
textCopyTerminal: Python full package          ← always
     ↓
Small cleared JSON only
     ↓
Optional: local Qwen (or your mini if it behaves)
     ↓
Never paste core/condensed/ledgers into agents
Bottom line: use the zip in your terminal with Python. Treat agents as token-hungry helpers, not the runtime. Mental model





















In Grok chatIn your terminalYou type a promptYou put text/JSON in subjectGrok repliesEngineers return final_verdict + allowed_for_llmConversation memoryLedger file under artifacts/

2. Interactive loop (closest to “typing into Grok”)
BashCopycd megacompact_uair_pipeline
python3
Then:
PythonCopyfrom engineers import DoublePassEngineerGate

gate = DoublePassEngineerGate(ledger_path="artifacts/my_chat_ledger.jsonl")
n = 0

while True:
    text = input("you> ").strip()
    if text in ("quit", "exit", "q"):
        break
    n += 1
    # treat free text as a plan by default
    subject = {"plan": text}
    subject_type = "plan"
    if text.lower().startswith("claim:"):
        subject = {"claim": text[6:].strip()}
        subject_type = "claim"
    r = gate.run(subject, subject_id=f"chat-{n}", subject_type=subject_type)
    d = r.to_dict()
    print("verdict:", d.get("final_verdict"), "| allowed_for_llm:", d.get("allowed_for_llm"))
    # optional: print issues
    for pass_name in ("stationary_pass_1", "non_stationary", "stationary_pass_2"):
        p = d.get(pass_name) or {}
        issues = p.get("issues") or []
        if issues:
            print(" ", pass_name, issues[:2])
Type plans/prompts as you would to Grok; type claim: ... for claim checks; quit to exit.

3. What to put in subject_type



































What you’re sendingsubject_typeShapeIdea / prompt / plan"plan"{"plan": "..."} or {"text": "..."}Product/safety claim"claim"{"claim": "..."}Source code"source"string of code, or {"path": "..."} + contextMarket-like event"NormalizedEvent"event dict with timestamps, etc.Decision / label"DecisionPacket" / "OutcomeLabel"schema-shaped dicts

4. How this differs from Grok chat

No free-form “conversation intelligence” in the gate — it checks integrity, causality, accounting, completeness language, etc.
Verdicts: PASS / ABSTAIN / BLOCKED, plus allowed_for_llm.
Memory: the ledger file, not chat history.
To run the pipeline (synth, labels, audit), use:BashCopypython run_all.py
# or
python pipeline.py stage synthThat is separate from “chat through engineers.”

Agent does software work. Engineers do gate work. Don’t expect the engineers REPL to replace Claude Code.

Your mini LLM vs small Qwen





















Use for coding agent?Qwen2.5-Coder (via Ollama)Yes — preferred for code/debugRandom mini on laptopOnly if it’s already a strong instruct/coder; usually worse than Qwen CoderCustom mini trained on MegaCompactNot highest potential for general coding; niche for routing/summarizing cleared JSON later
For “code, debug, everything Claude Code would do,” use Qwen2.5-Coder + Aider/Cline, not the MegaCompact mini path.

Token survival (agents still burn context)

Don’t paste whole core.py / condensed spine into the agent every turn
Point the agent at one file or one error
Run MegaCompact yourself; give the agent only short run_summary.json / error lines
Prefer aider with git so it sees diffs, not the entire tree every time

Bottom line

Local assistant that codes/debugs like Claude Code → Ollama + Qwen2.5-Coder + Aider (or Cline/Continue) — works offline after model download.
MegaCompact → keep as the verification pipeline, not the IDE agent.
Custom mini → not the path to Claude Code capability; Qwen Coder is the better fit for what you described.

Short version
Jarvis = local assistant (model + tools + router).
MegaCompact = not the brain — it’s a safety / verification module Jarvis calls, like an auditor.
Movie-Jarvis that knows everything and trades for you = out of scope / blocked.
Local tool-using assistant with MegaCompact as a spine = feasible.

How it would work together
textCopyYou (type or voice)
    ↓
Jarvis host (local Qwen/Ollama + tool router)
    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ code/debug  → Aider / shell / files     │  ← “Claude Code” work
│ plan/claim  → engineer_gate             │  ← MegaCompact
│ market-sim  → pipeline stages + gates   │  ← MegaCompact
│ summary     → only if allowed_for_llm   │  ← ClearedLLMGateway
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
Day-to-day

You talk to Jarvis (local model; offline after download).
Jarvis classifies intent: code | shell | research | sim | claim/plan.
Risky / claim / sim → DoublePassEngineerGate first.
Code/debug → local coding tools (no need for the full pipeline).
Pipeline → CLI stages; return short JSON only.
Model only sees cleared summaries.


Layers



































LayerWhatMegaCompact’s job1 RuntimeOllama, host process, optional voice—2 Agent/toolsAider, shell, filesRegister engineer + pipeline as tools3 Safety spineEngineers, gateway, SMT/interval, ledgersAll high-risk paths4 DomainPaper sim pipelineRun stages after policy5 MemoryLedgers, KSKB + human_confirmNot unlimited “soul” memory

Build path (engineers’ order)

Keep full MegaCompact package as canonical.
Thin Jarvis host: intent router + tool list.
Tools: engineer_run, pipeline_stage, adversarial, lab_ci, read_summary.
ClearedLLMGateway before the model sees domain artifacts.
Voice later (optional).
Do not train a mini-LLM as the Jarvis brain first — use Qwen-class local instruct + tools.


What this Jarvis must not be

World oracle / complete physics
Autonomous live trading
Silent override of engineers / abstention / SMT
Auto-promote facts into KSKB without human confirm


Honest scope

















FeasibleNot a valid product claimLocal assistant that codes, runs shell, and routes risk through MegaCompactOmniscient movie JarvisOnline or offline (local model + local Python)“It runs the market for you”

It searches for a folder that has both run_all.py and engineers.py, prints the path, saves it to megacompact_path.txt, and can run the program.
Usage
PowerShellCopy# Find only (prints path + how to run)
.\Find-And-Run-MegaCompact.ps1

If execution is blocked
PowerShellCopySet-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
.\Find-And-Run-MegaCompact.ps1 -Run
What it does

Searches under current dir, profile, Downloads, Documents, Desktop
Looks for megacompact_uair_pipeline or any dir with run_all.py + engineers.py
Prints PROJECT_PATH=...
Writes megacompact_path.txt in the current directory
With -Run, cds there and runs python run_all.py (or another -Command)

Option A — Paste this in PowerShell (no file needed)
Finds the project and prints the path:
PowerShellCopy$roots = @((Get-Location).Path, $env:USERPROFILE, "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads", "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents", "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop")
$hits = foreach ($r in $roots) {
  if (-not (Test-Path $r)) { continue }
  Get-ChildItem $r -Filter "run_all.py" -Recurse -Depth 8 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_.DirectoryName "engineers.py") } |
    ForEach-Object { $_.DirectoryName }
}
$hits = $hits | Select-Object -Unique
if (-not $hits) { Write-Host "Not found. Extract the zip first (Downloads)." -ForegroundColor Red }
else { $hits | ForEach-Object { Write-Host $_ -ForegroundColor Green }; $hits[0] | Set-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\megacompact_path.txt"; Write-Host "Saved: $env:USERPROFILE\megacompact_path.txt" }
Then, if it found a path:

Paste-only (no script file) — run this in PowerShell
PowerShellCopy$search = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "Downloads"
$dest   = Join-Path $search "MegaCompact"

$zip = Get-ChildItem $search -Filter "*megacompact*.zip" -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |
  Select-Object -First 1

if (-not $zip) {
  Write-Host "No *megacompact*.zip in Downloads. Put the zip there first." -ForegroundColor Red
} else {
  Write-Host "Zip: $($zip.FullName)" -ForegroundColor Cyan
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dest -Force | Out-Null
  Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $zip.FullName -DestinationPath $dest -Force
  $proj = Get-ChildItem $dest -Filter "run_all.py" -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_.DirectoryName "engineers.py") } |
    Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty DirectoryName
  if ($proj) {
    Write-Host "PROJECT_PATH=$proj" -ForegroundColor Green
    $proj | Set-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\megacompact_path.txt"
    Write-Host "Then:`n  cd `"$proj`"`n  python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`n  python run_all.py"
  } else {
    Write-Host "Extracted but run_all.py not found under $dest" -ForegroundColor Red
  }
}
Then:
PowerShellCopy$p = Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\megacompact_path.txt"
cd $p
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python run_all.py

PowerShellCopy$NeoPath = "C:\Users\AIAli\OneDrive\Desktop\NEO"
$out = Join-Path $NeoPath "_mini_llm_separated"
$kw = 'gguf|safetensors|ollama|lmstudio|lm-studio|qwen|llama|mistral|tokenizer|lora|vllm|huggingface|mini.?llm|modelfile|open-webui|gptq|awq'

Get-ChildItem $NeoPath -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { $_.FullName -notmatch '\\_mini_llm_separated\\' } |
  Where-Object {
    $b = ($_.FullName + ' ' + $_.Name).ToLower()
    $b -match $kw -or $_.Extension -match '\.(gguf|safetensors|pt|pth|onnx|ckpt)$'
  } |
  ForEach-Object {
    $rel = $_.FullName.Substring($NeoPath.Length).TrimStart('\')
    $target = Join-Path $out $rel
    $td = Split-Path $target -Parent
    if (-not (Test-Path $td)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $td -Force | Out-Null }
    Copy-Item $_.FullName $target -Force
    Write-Host "copied $rel"
  }

Write-Host "Done -> $out" -ForegroundColor Green

Practical recommendation
For a local assistant (chat / light coding help):

Prefer qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf (or SmolLM2 1.7B if you like it).
Run with llama.cpp / LM Studio / Ollama-style GGUF loader — you already have llama_cpp_local_smoke.py.
Treat mini_llm.py as your experiment script, not as “better than Qwen GGUF” until you prove it.

For MegaCompact: keep using Python run_all.py. Point any local model only at short cleared summaries, not the whole pipeline.
Cleanup later (optional): you can delete duplicate copies under kaggle_downloads_latest\workspace* once you’re happy with _mini_llm_separated.

EnoughNot requiredYou paste a short description of the APITraining on your full repoExamples of DoublePassEngineerGate.run(...)A custom mini-LLMYour goal in plain languageInternet access to “MegaCompact docs”
The engineers are normal Python:
PythonCopyfrom engineers import DoublePassEngineerGate
gate = DoublePassEngineerGate(ledger_path="artifacts/my_ledger.jsonl")
r = gate.run({"plan": "..."}, subject_id="x", subject_type="plan")
print(r.to_dict()["final_verdict"], r.allowed_for_llm)
Any competent model can write PowerShell/Python around that if you show it this pattern.
What goes wrong without context
If you only say “write scripts for the engineers” with no API snippet, the model may invent APIs, skip double-pass, or treat the model as the gate. That’s missing context in the prompt, not missing special training.
